A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same THESEUS work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including appendices A–F in v1 and A–G in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language transfer experiments, interpolation ablations, and fine-tuning convergence results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original summarization results, alignment diagnostics, and additional comparisons.

M1.justification: Table 3 adds a combined THESEUS + GradFix variant. The core Procrustes transport pipeline and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Expanded covariance-accumulation and depth-interpolation descriptions primarily document implementation rather than establish changes to the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds CNN/DailyMail summarization using Flan-T5 to T5-v1.1 transfer (Appendix E.3, Table 10), extending evaluation from classification to generative language output. The eight vision datasets and five entailment tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds evaluated Linear, Ortho, Linear-Ortho, and Pinv-Ortho transport baselines alongside existing pseudo-inverse methods. Table 3 adds THESEUS + GradFix comparisons, and Table 4 adds an interpolated-source control. Existing comparison methods remain represented.

E3.justification: New protocols include ROUGE-L summarization with 200/500/800 alignment samples and four scaling coefficients, fixed-scaling sensitivity tests, disjoint-validation activation comparisons, and norm-error evaluation. Table 1 extends vision alignment to B=50. The retained fine-tuning settings and existing few-shot protocols otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds scaling sensitivity, held-out activation alignment, and transport-operator ablations (Sections 4.5, 4.7, and Appendix G). It also examines damage caused by depth interpolation and adds computational/memory scaling analysis. These substantially extend the retained interpolation and warm-start analyses.

E5.justification: New Figure 2 shows shaded bands around accuracy curves, but neither its caption nor Section 4.5 defines their meaning. Neither PDF specifies run counts or seeds, so whether these bands introduce statistical uncertainty estimates or another kind of range remains unresolved.

E6.justification: Most retained benchmark accuracy entries match. v2 adds hybrid-method results, interpolation controls, B=50 vision accuracy of 69.48%, and Tables 10–11. New summarization results include ROUGE-L 0.1437 at D=800 and alpha=1 versus 0.1053 for the target baseline. New diagnostics report alignment improvements and transport norm errors.

T1.justification: v1's Appendix B injectivity lemma and Kronecker-product proof are removed; v2 instead invokes an aligned-subspace approximation in Appendix A. New Appendix B derives least-squares null-space ambiguity and constrained Procrustes trace maximization. Appendices D and G add complexity reasoning and formal alternative transport constructions.

C1.justification: The central contributions—functional task-vector transport, closed-form Procrustes alignment, and training-free transfer—remain intact. v2 qualifies the introduction's broad heterogeneous-model framing by explicitly focusing on Transformer variants differing in width, depth, and pretraining.

C2.justification: v2 newly qualifies the dependence on labeled validation data and explains that depth interpolation severely damages the source predictor. It interprets activation similarity as evidence of shared functional structure, connects scaling robustness to norm preservation, and argues that coupled operator matching is necessary beyond feature alignment.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code link, identifies transported and excluded modules, and documents token retention and streaming centered-covariance accumulation. Section 4.4 specifies the 12-to-24-layer interpolation procedure, coefficients, endpoint handling, and affected parameters. These resolve substantial implementation omissions in v1 without establishing that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix G explicitly position THESEUS against latent-space communication and semantic alignment, citing Moschella et al. and Maiorca et al. Additional references support task arithmetic, summarization, and ROUGE. The broader positioning relative to rebasin and training-based transfer remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites method motivation and experimental narratives, reduces repetitive explanations, and reorganizes the theoretical appendices. It moves the existing few-shot protocol into the main text and integrates additional analysis subsections. These changes extend beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 adds scaling-sensitivity, activation-similarity, and computational-scaling figures, plus summarization and alignment-ablation tables. Existing Tables 1, 3, and 4 gain rows. The original convergence figure is retained as Figure 3 with a revised caption and placement.

improvement.justification: The summarization experiment, practical qualifications, and implementation details provide useful gains over v1. However, new Appendix G gives Ortho and THESEUS the same displayed Procrustes construction while Table 11 reports different accuracies and norm errors, leaving its claimed evidence for the necessity of coupled matching unresolved. This substantive inconsistency in the added mechanistic argument prevents a reliable net-quality judgment despite the improvements elsewhere.
